title: API: Fee service - flat contribution fee collection and reserve deposit
body:
## Overview
Implement the platform fee model for Poolr. Fees are charged as a flat amount on each individual contribution at payment time - not as a percentage on the payout. This ensures the platform reserve starts building from the very first contribution in cycle 1, before any payout has gone out, which is when the reserve is needed most.

## Why contribution-based fees, not payout-based
If Poolr charged a fee only on payouts, the reserve would be empty during the early cycles of every group - exactly when a default is most damaging. A contribution-based fee means reserve accumulation is proportional to risk exposure from day one. It also distributes the cost across all contributing members rather than concentrating it on the payout recipient.

## Fee structure

### Flat fee tiers (configurable via environment variables)
| Contribution amount | Platform fee |
|---|---|
| Under NGN 10,000 | NGN 100 flat |
| NGN 10,000 - NGN 50,000 | NGN 200 flat |
| Above NGN 50,000 | NGN 400 flat |

### Fee split
- 20% of every fee collected goes to the platform protection reserve
- 80% goes to Poolr operating revenue
- Example: NGN 200 fee on a NGN 20,000 contribution - NGN 40 to reserve, NGN 160 to revenue

### What the member pays
- Paystack path: member pays `contribution_amount + fee_amount` in a single Paystack transaction
- Wallet path: wallet is debited `contribution_amount + fee_amount` in a single operation
- The fee is shown clearly to the member before they confirm payment

## Schema changes

### New `ContributionFee` table
Tracks every fee collected at contribution time.
```
ContributionFee {
  id               uuid PK
  contribution_id  uuid FK -> Contribution  UNIQUE
  user_id          uuid FK -> User
  contribution_amount int    -- the contribution amount in kobo
  fee_amount          int    -- total platform fee charged in kobo
  reserve_amount      int    -- 20% of fee_amount (deposited to reserve)
  revenue_amount      int    -- 80% of fee_amount (operating revenue)
  created_at          timestamp
}
```

### Update `Contribution` model
- Add `fee_amount` (int) -- the platform fee charged for this contribution, stored for quick reference without joining ContributionFee
- Add `total_charged` (int) -- contribution_amount + fee_amount (what Paystack actually charged or what was debited from wallet)

## Tasks

### FeeService
- [ ] Create `FeeService` in `src/modules/payments/fee.service.ts`
- [ ] `FeeService.calculateFee(contributionAmountKobo: number): number` -- returns the flat fee for the given contribution amount based on configured tiers. Reads tiers from environment config, not hardcoded.
- [ ] `FeeService.collectFee(contributionId, userId, contributionAmount)` -- called atomically with contribution PAID status update:
  - Calculate fee using `calculateFee()`
  - Split into `reserve_amount` (20%) and `revenue_amount` (80%)
  - Create `ContributionFee` record
  - Call `ReserveService.deposit(reserveAmount, contributionFeeId)` to deposit reserve slice
  - All within the same Prisma `$transaction` as the contribution status update
- [ ] `FeeService.getFeeSummary(filters)` -- returns total fees collected, reserve contributions, and revenue; filterable by date range and group_id

### Integration with contribution flow
- [ ] Update `PaymentsService.initiateContribution()` to:
  - Call `FeeService.calculateFee(contributionAmount)` before creating Paystack transaction
  - Set Paystack transaction amount to `contribution_amount + fee_amount`
  - Return `{ checkout_url, contribution_amount, fee_amount, total_amount }` in the API response
- [ ] Update `PaymentsService.handleChargeSuccess()` (webhook handler) to:
  - Call `FeeService.collectFee()` atomically with marking contribution PAID
  - Never call `FeeService.collectFee()` twice for the same contribution (idempotency check via `ContributionFee.contribution_id` UNIQUE constraint)
- [ ] Update wallet-funded contribution path:
  - Total wallet debit = `contribution_amount + fee_amount`
  - `WalletService.debit()` call uses `total_charged` not just `contribution_amount`
  - `can-pay` check: `wallet.balance >= contribution_amount + fee_amount`
  - After wallet debit, call `FeeService.collectFee()` to record fee and deposit to reserve

### Payout processor - confirm no fee deduction
- [ ] Explicitly confirm `PayoutProcessor` sends the full pooled contribution amount to the recipient with zero fee deduction
- [ ] Add a code comment in `PayoutProcessor` referencing this ticket to prevent future confusion

### Configuration
- [ ] Add to `.env.example`:
  ```
  CONTRIBUTION_FEE_TIER_1_MAX=1000000
  CONTRIBUTION_FEE_TIER_1_AMOUNT=10000
  CONTRIBUTION_FEE_TIER_2_MAX=5000000
  CONTRIBUTION_FEE_TIER_2_AMOUNT=20000
  CONTRIBUTION_FEE_TIER_3_AMOUNT=40000
  RESERVE_CONTRIBUTION_PERCENTAGE=0.20
  ```
- [ ] All fee tiers configurable without a code deploy

### Admin endpoints
- [ ] `GET /admin/fees` -- total fees collected, reserve contributions, operating revenue; filterable by date range and group
- [ ] `GET /admin/fees/:contributionFeeId` -- single fee record detail

### Tests
- [ ] Unit test `calculateFee()`: boundary values at tier 1/2/3 thresholds, exact tier boundary amounts
- [ ] Unit test `collectFee()`: correct split calculation, idempotency (second call for same contribution throws/is ignored)
- [ ] Integration test: Paystack checkout amount equals contribution + fee
- [ ] Integration test: wallet debit equals contribution + fee
- [ ] Integration test: payout sends full pooled amount, no deduction

## Acceptance criteria
- Fee is collected at contribution time, never at payout time
- Paystack checkout amount equals `contribution_amount + fee_amount` exactly
- `FeeService.collectFee()` and contribution PAID status update are always atomic - no contribution can be marked PAID without a corresponding `ContributionFee` record
- A duplicate `charge.success` webhook for the same contribution does NOT create a second `ContributionFee` record (idempotent)
- Wallet-funded contributions also collect the fee - no fee-free path exists
- `can-pay` wallet check accounts for the fee amount
- All fee configuration is changeable without a code deploy
- Payout processor sends full amount to recipient with zero deduction
- Admin can view total revenue and reserve contributions from fee collection

## Related tickets
- Depends on #8 (Payments module - contribution flow and webhook handler)
- Depends on #12 (Wallet module - WalletService.debit())
- Required by #55 (Updated reserve - deposit now triggered by FeeService, not PayoutProcessor)
- Required by #26 (Wallet-funded contributions - can-pay check must include fee)

title: API: Platform reserve - updated to be funded by contribution fees (replaces payout-based funding)
body:
## Overview
Update the platform protection reserve (originally specified in ticket #50) to reflect the revised fee model. The reserve is now funded by a 20% slice of every contribution fee (ticket #54), not by a percentage of payout transaction fees. This ticket also clarifies the two distinct drawdown scenarios and adds the `ContributionFee` FK to `ReserveTransaction`.

## What changed from ticket #50
- `ReserveService.deposit()` is now called by `FeeService.collectFee()` (at contribution time) instead of by `PayoutProcessor` (at payout time)
- `ReserveTransaction` now references `contribution_fee_id` (FK to `ContributionFee`) instead of `payout_id` (FK to `Payout`) for DEPOSIT transactions
- The `ReserveTransactionType` enum replaces the old DEPOSIT type with DEPOSIT_FROM_FEE for clarity
- All other reserve logic (drawdowns, replenishment, admin endpoints) is unchanged from ticket #50

## Two reserve drawdown scenarios (unchanged)

### Scenario 1 - Missed contribution shortfall
When a member misses a contribution, the recipient's payout goes out in full. The reserve covers the missed contribution amount. A `Debt` record is created (ticket #47) and the reserve is replenished when the defaulter clears their debt.

### Scenario 2 - Net-positive removed member refund
When a member is removed with net_position <= 0 (contributed more than received), their net refund is credited to their Poolr Wallet on their original payout date. The reserve funds this refund, linked to the outstanding debt record, and is replenished when the debt is cleared.

## Schema changes

### New `PlatformReserve` table (singleton - one row)
```
PlatformReserve {
  id         uuid PK
  balance    int        -- current reserve balance in kobo
  updated_at timestamp
}
```

### New `ReserveTransaction` table
```
ReserveTransaction {
  id                  uuid PK
  type                ReserveTransactionType
  amount              int
  debt_id             uuid? FK -> Debt             -- set for DRAWDOWN_SHORTFALL, DRAWDOWN_REFUND, REPLENISHMENT
  contribution_fee_id uuid? FK -> ContributionFee  -- set for DEPOSIT_FROM_FEE
  group_member_id     uuid? FK -> GroupMember       -- set for DRAWDOWN_REFUND
  balance_after       int                           -- running reserve balance after this transaction
  created_at          timestamp
}
```

### Updated enum
```
enum ReserveTransactionType {
  DEPOSIT_FROM_FEE     -- 20% slice of a contribution fee, deposited at contribution time
  DRAWDOWN_SHORTFALL   -- covers a missed contribution so recipient payout goes out
  DRAWDOWN_REFUND      -- covers a net-positive removed member refund on their original payout date
  REPLENISHMENT        -- defaulter cleared their debt, reserve restored
}
```

## Tasks

### ReserveService
- [ ] Create `ReserveService` in `src/modules/payments/reserve.service.ts`
- [ ] `ReserveService.deposit(reserveAmount, contributionFeeId)` -- called by `FeeService.collectFee()` after each confirmed contribution. Creates `ReserveTransaction` of type DEPOSIT_FROM_FEE. All within the same Prisma `$transaction` as fee collection and contribution status update.
- [ ] `ReserveService.drawdownShortfall(amount, debtId)` -- called by `PenaltyService` when a missed contribution is covered. Debits reserve, creates DRAWDOWN_SHORTFALL transaction.
- [ ] `ReserveService.drawdownRefund(amount, debtId, groupMemberId)` -- called by `RefundProcessor` on the removed member's original payout date. Debits reserve, creates DRAWDOWN_REFUND transaction.
- [ ] `ReserveService.replenish(amount, debtId)` -- called by `DebtClearanceService` when a defaulter clears their debt. Credits reserve, creates REPLENISHMENT transaction. Reserve is replenished before any creditor reimbursements.
- [ ] `ReserveService.getBalance()` -- returns current reserve balance in kobo.
- [ ] All balance mutations use Prisma `$transaction` with a SELECT FOR UPDATE pattern to prevent race conditions on concurrent deposits or drawdowns.
- [ ] On any drawdown where the debit would bring balance below zero: proceed with drawdown (do not block), fire a Sentry critical alert immediately with: drawdown type, amount, current balance, shortfall amount, and linked debt_id.

### Configuration
- [ ] `RESERVE_CONTRIBUTION_PERCENTAGE=0.20` -- percentage of each contribution fee deposited to reserve. Configurable without a code deploy. Read by `FeeService.collectFee()` when splitting fee into reserve and revenue slices.

### Admin endpoints
- [ ] `GET /admin/reserve` -- current balance; all-time totals: deposited, drawn down (shortfall), drawn down (refunds), replenished
- [ ] `GET /admin/reserve/transactions` -- paginated `ReserveTransaction` list with type labels, linked contribution fee or debt details, and running balance
- [ ] `GET /admin/reserve/health` -- reserve health report:
  - Current balance
  - Total outstanding debt exposure (sum of all OUTSTANDING Debt.total_owed)
  - Coverage ratio (balance / exposure)
  - Warning flag if coverage ratio < 50%
  - Estimated months until reserve is exhausted at current drawdown rate
- [ ] `GET /admin/reserve/pending-refunds` -- list of scheduled DRAWDOWN_REFUND jobs with amount and scheduled date, so admin can anticipate upcoming reserve needs

### Tests
- [ ] Unit test `deposit()`: balance increments correctly, DEPOSIT_FROM_FEE transaction created with correct contributionFeeId
- [ ] Unit test `drawdownShortfall()`: balance decrements correctly, DRAWDOWN_SHORTFALL transaction created
- [ ] Unit test `drawdownRefund()`: balance decrements correctly, DRAWDOWN_REFUND transaction created with groupMemberId
- [ ] Unit test `replenish()`: balance increments correctly, REPLENISHMENT transaction created
- [ ] Unit test concurrent deposits: no race condition, final balance is correct
- [ ] Unit test drawdown below zero: proceeds, Sentry alert fired, balance_after is negative (allowed)

## Acceptance criteria
- Reserve balance is funded exclusively from contribution fees (20% slice), never from payout processing
- `deposit()` is always called within the same Prisma `$transaction` as `FeeService.collectFee()` - no fee is collected without a corresponding reserve deposit
- Reserve balance is always consistent with the sum of all `ReserveTransaction` amounts
- Concurrent deposits do not cause race conditions
- A drawdown below zero does NOT block the payout or refund - it fires a Sentry critical alert within 60 seconds
- `DEPOSIT_FROM_FEE` and both `DRAWDOWN` types are clearly distinguishable in the admin transaction log
- Admin health endpoint flags when coverage ratio drops below 50%
- `RESERVE_CONTRIBUTION_PERCENTAGE` is changeable without a code deploy

## Related tickets
- Depends on #54 (Fee service - deposit() called from FeeService.collectFee())
- Depends on #47 (Debt tracking - debt_id FK on drawdown transactions)
- Required by #49 (Debt clearance - replenish() called on debt clearance)
- Required by #52 (Group removal - drawdownRefund() called by RefundProcessor)
- Supersedes the reserve funding model described in #50 (fee source changed from payout to contribution)

title: API: Update ticket #52 - refund formula removes processing fee deduction
body:
## Overview
Amends the refund calculation logic defined in ticket #52 (missed contribution escalation and group removal). The original formula deducted a 2% processing fee from the removed member's refund. This has been removed - the refund is now simply the member's total contributions minus their outstanding debt, with no additional deduction.

## What changes

### Original formula (ticket #52)
```
refund_amount = total_contributions_made - outstanding_debt - processing_fee (2%)
```

### Corrected formula (this ticket)
```
refund_amount = total_contributions_made - outstanding_debt
```

## Rationale
The removed member has already paid the platform fee on every contribution they made (ticket #54). Deducting an additional 2% processing fee on exit would mean penalising an honest contributor twice - once for each contribution they made in good faith, and again when the platform is returning their own money. The contribution fee already funds the reserve and platform operations. No further deduction is justified.

## Affected code paths in ticket #52

### GroupsService.removeMemberForDefault()
- [ ] Update `refund_amount` calculation: remove the 2% processing fee deduction
- [ ] New formula: `refund_amount = total_contributions_made - outstanding_debt`
- [ ] If `outstanding_debt >= total_contributions_made`: `refund_amount = 0`, no refund job scheduled
- [ ] If `outstanding_debt < total_contributions_made`: `refund_amount > 0`, schedule BullMQ refund job for original payout date

### GroupMember model (confirm no schema change needed)
- [ ] `GroupMember.refund_amount` stores the corrected value (no 2% deduction)
- [ ] No schema migration required - same field, updated calculation

### Notifications
- [ ] Update notification text sent to removed member on removal:
  - Old: "Outstanding debt of NGN [debt] and a 2% processing fee have been deducted"
  - New: "Your outstanding debt of NGN [debt] has been deducted"
- [ ] Update notification text when refund_amount <= 0:
  - Old: "After deducting your outstanding debt and a processing fee, no refund is due"
  - New: "After deducting your outstanding debt of NGN [debt], no refund is due"

## Tests to update
- [ ] Update unit tests in `GroupsService.removeMemberForDefault()` to reflect corrected refund formula
- [ ] Add specific test case: member with total_contributions = outstanding_debt should get refund_amount = 0
- [ ] Add test case: member with total_contributions > outstanding_debt should get refund_amount = difference (no further deduction)

## Acceptance criteria
- `refund_amount` equals `total_contributions_made - outstanding_debt` exactly, with no additional deductions
- No removed member is charged a processing or exit fee on top of their outstanding debt
- All notification text references to processing fees are removed
- Unit tests pass with the corrected formula

## Related tickets
- Amends #52 (Missed contribution escalation and group removal - refund scheduling)
- No dependency on #54 (Fee service) beyond the rationale - fee collection happens upstream at contribution time

title: API + Web + Mobile: Update contribution flow to display platform fee before payment confirmation
body:
## Overview
Update the contribution payment flow across API, web, and mobile to clearly show the platform fee to the member before they confirm payment. This covers both the Paystack checkout path and the wallet-funded path. Also updates the wallet balance check to account for the fee amount.

## Context
With the contribution-based fee model (ticket #54), every member pays a flat fee on top of their contribution amount. The member must see this fee clearly before confirming - not discover it after the fact on their bank statement. Transparency here is critical for trust in a financial app.

## API changes

### POST /payments/contribute/:cycleId - updated response
Add fee details to the contribution initiation response:
```typescript
// Updated ContributeResponseDto
{
  payment_source: 'PAYSTACK' | 'WALLET';
  contribution_amount: number;  // in kobo - the group contribution
  fee_amount: number;           // in kobo - Poolr platform flat fee
  total_amount: number;         // contribution_amount + fee_amount
  checkout_url?: string;        // present only for PAYSTACK payment source
}
```
- [ ] Update `PaymentsController` and `PaymentsService.initiateContribution()` to call `FeeService.calculateFee()` and include `fee_amount` and `total_amount` in the response before creating the Paystack transaction
- [ ] Paystack transaction is initialized with `total_amount` (not just `contribution_amount`)

### GET /wallet/can-pay/:cycleId - updated check
- [ ] Update can-pay check to verify `wallet.balance >= contribution_amount + fee_amount`
- [ ] Update can-pay response to include `fee_amount` and `total_amount` alongside `can_pay: boolean`
```typescript
// Updated CanPayResponseDto
{
  can_pay: boolean;
  wallet_balance: number;
  contribution_amount: number;
  fee_amount: number;
  total_amount: number;
}
```

## Web changes (extends ticket #20)

### Paystack path
- [ ] Before redirecting to Paystack checkout, show a confirmation modal or summary card:
  - "Contribution: NGN [contribution_amount]"
  - "Platform fee: NGN [fee_amount]"
  - "Total: NGN [total_amount]"
  - "Pay NGN [total_amount]" CTA button
  - "Cancel" link
- [ ] Only redirect to Paystack checkout after user taps the confirm CTA

### Wallet path
- [ ] "Pay from Wallet" button is shown only when `wallet.balance >= total_amount` (contribution + fee)
- [ ] Show the same fee breakdown summary before deducting from wallet:
  - "Contribution: NGN [contribution_amount]"
  - "Platform fee: NGN [fee_amount]"
  - "Total deducted from Poolr Wallet: NGN [total_amount]"
  - "Confirm" CTA
- [ ] If wallet balance covers contribution but not contribution + fee, show the wallet option as disabled with a tooltip: "Insufficient wallet balance. Top up NGN [shortfall] to pay from wallet."

## Mobile changes (extends ticket #25)

### Paystack path
- [ ] Show a native bottom sheet or modal with fee breakdown before opening Paystack in `expo-web-browser`
- [ ] Same fields: contribution amount, fee amount, total, confirm and cancel actions

### Wallet path
- [ ] Same logic as web: show only when balance >= total_amount, display fee breakdown before confirming
- [ ] Disabled wallet option shows tooltip/helper text explaining the shortfall

## UX copy guidelines
- Use "Platform fee" not "Transaction fee" or "Service charge" - consistent with in-app language
- Display amounts in NGN with comma-separated thousands (e.g. "NGN 20,000" not "NGN 20000")
- Never show amounts in kobo to the user - always convert before display
- The fee breakdown must be shown before every contribution payment, not just the first time

## Tests
- [ ] API: `POST /payments/contribute/:cycleId` response includes `fee_amount` and `total_amount`
- [ ] API: Paystack transaction is initialized with `total_amount`
- [ ] API: `GET /wallet/can-pay/:cycleId` returns false when `wallet.balance >= contribution_amount` but `wallet.balance < total_amount`
- [ ] Web: fee breakdown is rendered before redirect to Paystack
- [ ] Web: wallet option disabled and shows helper text when balance covers contribution but not total
- [ ] Mobile: bottom sheet renders with correct fee amounts before Paystack browser opens

## Acceptance criteria
- Every member sees the fee breakdown (contribution + fee + total) before confirming any payment on both web and mobile
- No member is charged more than `total_amount` shown in the breakdown
- Wallet can-pay check uses `total_amount`, not just `contribution_amount`
- Wallet option is disabled (not hidden) when balance is between `contribution_amount` and `total_amount`, with a clear explanation
- Fee amounts are always displayed in NGN, never in kobo
- Paystack checkout is initialized with `total_amount` exactly

## Related tickets
- Depends on #54 (Fee service - calculateFee() and fee amounts in contribution response)
- Extends #20 (Web: Contribution payment flow)
- Extends #25 (Mobile: Home, Groups, and Contribution screens)
- Extends #26 (Wallet-funded contributions - can-pay check updated)

title: Compliance: Update legal review scope - fee charged on contributions not payouts
body:
## Overview
Amends the legal review scope defined in ticket #32 to reflect the updated fee model. The original ticket asked legal counsel to confirm that charging a 1% fee on payouts is permissible. The fee model has changed to a flat fee charged on each contribution. This is a meaningful regulatory distinction and legal counsel must specifically advise on the contribution-time fee structure.

## What changed from ticket #32

### Original item (ticket #32)
> Transaction fee: confirm that charging a 1% fee on payouts is permissible under current CBN guidelines.

### Updated item (this ticket)
Legal counsel must now advise on:
- [ ] Confirm that charging a flat platform fee per contribution (not on payouts) is permissible under current CBN guidelines
- [ ] Advise whether charging fees at contribution time vs payout time changes the regulatory classification of Poolr under CBN payment service rules - specifically whether collecting fees on inflows (contributions) triggers different licensing requirements than collecting on outflows (payouts)
- [ ] Confirm that Poolr can collect the platform fee as part of the same Paystack transaction as the member's contribution (i.e. member pays contribution + fee in one Paystack charge, Poolr receives both and internally splits them)
- [ ] Advise on the correct accounting treatment for the fee split: 20% to reserve, 80% to operating revenue - specifically whether the reserve constitutes a regulated "customer fund" or is simply a business expense reserve
- [ ] Confirm the flat fee tier structure (NGN 100 / 200 / 400 based on contribution size) does not constitute a percentage-based fee that would require different disclosure or regulatory treatment

## Context for legal counsel
Poolr charges a flat platform fee on each group contribution, collected at payment time. The fee is split internally: 20% goes to a platform protection reserve (used to guarantee payouts when a member defaults), and 80% goes to platform operating revenue. The member pays the contribution amount plus the fee in a single Paystack transaction. The payout recipient receives the full pooled contribution amount with no deduction.

## Deliverable
- [ ] Written legal opinion covering all five updated items above
- [ ] Specific confirmation or flag on whether contribution-time fee collection requires any different CBN disclosure, licensing, or approval compared to payout-time fee collection

## Acceptance criteria
- Legal opinion explicitly addresses contribution-time fee collection (not just fee collection generally)
- Legal opinion addresses the regulatory treatment of the 20% reserve fund
- Any new licensing or disclosure requirements identified are filed as separate GitHub issues

## Related tickets
- Amends #32 (Engage a Nigerian fintech lawyer for regulatory review)
- Context from #54 (Fee service) and #55 (Reserve)

title: API: Update trust score Elite perk - zero contribution fees for one group per month
body:
## Overview
Amends the Elite tier perk defined in ticket #43 (Trust score system). The original perk stated "zero platform fees on one group per month". With the updated contribution-based fee model, this is now correctly framed as "zero contribution fees for one group per month" - meaning Poolr waives the per-contribution platform fee for all contributions made within one nominated group per month for Elite users.

## What changed from ticket #43

### Original Elite perk
> 80-100 (Elite): Unlimited group size, zero platform fees on one group per month, priority payout scheduling

### Updated Elite perk
> 80-100 (Elite): Unlimited group size, zero contribution fees for one group per month (Poolr covers the fee for every contribution the Elite user makes in their nominated group that month), priority payout scheduling

## Implementation detail

### How the perk works
- An Elite user nominates one group per month where the fee waiver applies
- For every contribution the Elite user makes in that nominated group during the calendar month, `FeeService.collectFee()` sets `fee_amount = 0` for that contribution
- Poolr absorbs the cost - no reserve deposit for waived fees
- The user can change their nominated group once per month
- The perk applies only to the Elite user's own contributions - not to other members of the same group

### Schema changes
- [ ] Add `FeeWaiver` table:
```
FeeWaiver {
  id           uuid PK
  user_id      uuid FK -> User
  group_id     uuid FK -> Group
  month        date              -- first day of the calendar month this waiver applies to
  created_at   timestamp
  UNIQUE(user_id, month)         -- one waiver per user per month
}
```

### FeeService update
- [ ] Update `FeeService.calculateFee(contributionAmountKobo, userId, groupId, month)` to check for an active `FeeWaiver` for this user/group/month combination
- [ ] If a waiver exists: return `fee_amount = 0`, skip reserve deposit, create `ContributionFee` with `fee_amount = 0` (for audit trail)
- [ ] If no waiver: standard fee tier calculation unchanged

### New endpoints
- [ ] `POST /users/me/fee-waiver` -- Elite user nominates a group for fee waiver for the current month. Body: `{ group_id }`. Returns 403 if user is not Elite tier. Returns 400 if waiver already set for this month.
- [ ] `GET /users/me/fee-waiver` -- returns the current month's nominated group and fee waiver status

### Trust score integration
- [ ] In `TrustScoreService`, when a user crosses into Elite tier (score >= 80), send a push + in-app notification: "You have reached Elite status. Nominate a group to enjoy zero contribution fees this month."

## Tests
- [ ] `calculateFee()` returns 0 for Elite user with active waiver for the correct group and month
- [ ] `calculateFee()` returns normal fee for Elite user whose waiver is for a different group
- [ ] `calculateFee()` returns normal fee for Elite user after their waiver month has passed
- [ ] `POST /users/me/fee-waiver` returns 403 for non-Elite users
- [ ] `POST /users/me/fee-waiver` returns 400 on second call for the same month

## Acceptance criteria
- Elite user pays zero platform fee on all contributions in their nominated group for the nominated month
- Non-Elite users are never granted fee waivers
- A waived contribution creates a `ContributionFee` record with `fee_amount = 0` for audit trail
- Reserve is NOT funded from waived fees (Poolr absorbs the cost)
- User can update their nominated group once per month but cannot change it twice
- Fee waiver expires automatically at month end with no manual intervention

## Related tickets
- Amends #43 (Trust score system - Elite perk definition)
- Depends on #54 (Fee service - FeeService.calculateFee() must accept waiver check params)

title: API: Update B2B billing type enum from TRANSACTION_FEE to CONTRIBUTION_FEE
body:
## Overview
Small amendment to ticket #44 (B2B cooperative and corporate group onboarding). The `Organisation.billing_type` enum used `TRANSACTION_FEE` to describe the standard per-transaction fee model. With the revised fee structure charging on contributions (not transactions broadly), this enum value is renamed to `CONTRIBUTION_FEE` for accuracy and clarity.

## What changed from ticket #44

### Original schema
```
Organisation {
  billing_type  enum  -- TRANSACTION_FEE | FLAT_MONTHLY
}
```

### Updated schema
```
Organisation {
  billing_type  enum  -- CONTRIBUTION_FEE | FLAT_MONTHLY
}
```

## Enum definition update
```
enum OrgBillingType {
  CONTRIBUTION_FEE  -- standard Poolr flat fee per contribution (fee tiers from FeeService)
  FLAT_MONTHLY      -- negotiated flat monthly rate for the organisation, no per-contribution fee
}
```

## Behaviour clarification

### CONTRIBUTION_FEE orgs
- Standard fee tier applies to every contribution made by a member of an organisation-owned group
- Fee calculated by `FeeService.calculateFee()` exactly as for non-organisation groups
- No special treatment - this is the default

### FLAT_MONTHLY orgs
- Organisation pays a negotiated flat monthly fee (stored in `Organisation.monthly_fee`)
- Per-contribution fee is waived for all members of all groups under this organisation
- `FeeService.calculateFee()` returns 0 for contributions in FLAT_MONTHLY organisation groups
- Poolr invoices the organisation directly for `monthly_fee` at the start of each month
- A new `OrgInvoice` table tracks monthly invoices and payment status

## Schema changes

### Update `Organisation` model (from ticket #44)
- Rename `billing_type` enum value `TRANSACTION_FEE` to `CONTRIBUTION_FEE`
- Add `monthly_fee` (int, nullable) -- monthly flat fee in kobo; required when billing_type = FLAT_MONTHLY

### New `OrgInvoice` table (FLAT_MONTHLY orgs only)
```
OrgInvoice {
  id              uuid PK
  organisation_id uuid FK -> Organisation
  month           date          -- first day of the billed month
  amount          int           -- monthly_fee in kobo
  status          InvoiceStatus -- PENDING | PAID | OVERDUE
  paystack_ref    string?       -- set when paid
  issued_at       timestamp
  paid_at         timestamp?
}

enum InvoiceStatus { PENDING PAID OVERDUE }
```
